precepts.text: Azariah is named Uzziah, the same king given in greater detail in Chronicles.
precepts.point: Azariah's fuller history is written elsewhere, and the teacher directs the reader to 2 Chronicles 26 for a more detailed account of his life and acts.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

precepts.why:
“Then all the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in the room of his father Amaziah.”

Azariah is Uzziah. Kings says Azariah son of Amaziah was sixteen years old when he began to reign; Chronicles names the same king Uzziah and gives his life and acts in greater detail. Kings itself points there: “are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?” For the fuller account of the king who did right, left the high places standing, and was smitten a leper, read 2 Chronicles 26.

precepts.text: Pride goeth before destruction; the brother became prideful and high, and it brought him to a fall.
precepts.point: The lesson to all of us is to stay in the spirit, stay humble, and never forget who put you in the position you are in. When a man becomes lifted up he loses his humility and forgets who set him where he is. Uzziah was a leper to the day of his death and dwelt in a separate house, cut off from the house of the Most High.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 26: Uzziah Prospers, Then Pride Brings Him Low

precepts.why:
“Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.” The brother became prideful and high, and it brought him to a fall.

“But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction”. Uzziah went into the temple to burn incense upon the altar of incense, which was not his office. When the priests withstood him, “Uzziah was wroth”, and while he was wroth, with a censer in his hand, “the leprosy even rose up in his forehead before the priests”. He “was a leper unto the day of his death, and dwelt in a several house”, “cut off from the house of the Lord”.

The lesson to all of us is to stay in the spirit, stay humble, and never forget who put you in the position you are in. When a man becomes lifted up he loses his humility and forgets who set him where he is.

precepts.text: The king was to write himself a copy of the law and read in it all his life, that he learn to fear the Most High and not lift himself above his brethren.
precepts.point: The lesson to all of us is to stay in the spirit, stay humble, and never forget who put you in the position you are in. When a man becomes lifted up he loses his humility and forgets who set him where he is. Uzziah was a leper to the day of his death and dwelt in a separate house, cut off from the house of the Most High.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 26: Uzziah Prospers, Then Pride Brings Him Low

precepts.why:
The law set the king’s duty plainly: “when he sitteth upon the throne of his kingdom, that he shall write him a copy of this law in a book out of that which is before the priests the Levites: And it shall be with him, and he shall read therein all the days of his life: that he may learn to fear the Lord his God, to keep all the words of this law and these statutes, to do them”.

The king was to write himself a copy of the law and read in it all his life, that he learn to fear the Most High and not lift himself above his brethren. Uzziah did the opposite: “his heart was lifted up to his destruction: for he transgressed against the Lord his God”. Had he kept the law before him, he would have known the incense was not his to burn.

precepts.text: The priesthood was given to Aaron and his sons as a gift; the stranger that came near was to be put to death, so the office was never the king's to seize.
precepts.point: The lesson to all of us is to stay in the spirit, stay humble, and never forget who put you in the position you are in. When a man becomes lifted up he loses his humility and forgets who set him where he is. Uzziah was a leper to the day of his death and dwelt in a separate house, cut off from the house of the Most High.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 26: Uzziah Prospers, Then Pride Brings Him Low

precepts.why:
The Most High said to Aaron, “thou and thy sons with thee shall keep your priest’s office for every thing of the altar, and within the vail”, and “I have given your priest’s office unto you as a service of gift: and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death.” The priesthood was given to Aaron and his sons as a gift, and the office was never the king’s to seize.

That is what Azariah and the fourscore priests told Uzziah: “It appertaineth not unto thee, Uzziah, to burn incense unto the Lord, but to the priests the sons of Aaron, that are consecrated to burn incense: go out of the sanctuary; for thou hast trespassed”. He came nigh where he did not belong, and “the Lord had smitten him.”

moments.label: The Mind of a Child: Void of Ego and Pride
The Mind of a Child: Void of Ego and Pride

points: Then all the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in the room of his father Amaziah. So he was sixteen years old. He was a novice.

note.label: The Mind of a Child: Void of Ego and Pride

points: He built Eloth, and restored it to Judah, after that the king slept with his fathers. Sixteen years old was Uzziah when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty and two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name also was Jecoliah of Jerusalem.

note.label: The Mind of a Child: Void of Ego and Pride

points: And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his father Amaziah did.

note.label: The Mind of a Child: Void of Ego and Pride

points: And he sought God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the visions of God: and as long as he sought the Lord, God made him to prosper. Zechariah was a prophet. He sought God when Zechariah was around — meaning who was helping him? God had the right men around this young man to tutor him and to guide him. He was a young king, but he prospered once he sought the Lord.

note.label: The Mind of a Child: Void of Ego and Pride

points: And he went forth and warred against the Philistines, and brake down the wall of Gath, and the wall of Jabneh, and the wall of Ashdod, and built cities about Ashdod, and among the Philistines.

note.label: The Mind of a Child: Void of Ego and Pride

points: And God helped him against the Philistines, and against the Arabians that dwelt in Gurbaal, and the Mehunims.

note.label: The Mind of a Child: Void of Ego and Pride

points: And the Ammonites gave gifts to Uzziah: and his name spread abroad even to the entering in of Egypt; for he strengthened himself exceedingly. So his name spread abroad — he became famous. The same way some of you leaders in here, people are going to hear about you. You will become famous. The Lord is going to deal with you and you will become famous.

note.label: The Mind of a Child: Void of Ego and Pride

points: But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction. When it says his heart was lifted up, he became prideful, highminded. That is where Paul got it from — not a novice, lest he be lifted up with pride and fall into the condemnation of the devil. Because this king was young. He had counsellors, and once that counsellor was not around any more, he started doing stupid stuff. Satan was messing with him.

Was God dealing with him? Yes, when he sought him. So he got lifted up. He was winning wars, he did a lot of great things in Israel, but now he got lifted up. He became arrogant. He thought he knew everything. Nobody could correct him. All those spirits of pride that we read about, the negative aspects, fell on him. In the beginning it was not there, but as time went on it grew.

For he transgressed against the Lord his God, and went into the temple of the Lord to burn incense upon the altar of incense. He went outside what God commanded him to do. He said, the Lord is dealing with me, so let me go and burn incense unto the Lord.

So what I am showing you is how God lifted up this brother, and when the Lord lifted him up he did so much great things in Israel — until he was lifted up unto his own destruction, meaning pride and arrogance started getting to him. He started thinking of himself more than he ought to.

note.label: The Mind of a Child: Void of Ego and Pride

points: And Azariah the priest went in after him, and with him fourscore priests of the Lord, that were valiant men: and they withstood Uzziah the king, and said unto him, It appertaineth not unto thee, Uzziah, to burn incense unto the Lord, but to the priests the sons of Aaron, that are consecrated to burn incense: go out of the sanctuary; for thou hast trespassed; neither shall it be for thine honour from the Lord God. So he does not want to listen to anybody. The high priest said, what are you doing, that is wrong. And he said, to hell with you, I am the king and God is dealing with me too, I want to burn incense unto my God.

note.label: The Mind of a Child: Void of Ego and Pride

points: Then Uzziah was wroth, and had a censer in his hand to burn incense: and while he was wroth with the priests, the leprosy even rose up in his forehead before the priests in the house of the Lord, from beside the incense altar. He was angry at them and said, I am going to burn incense, I do not care what you say. Remember, pride is when you do not want to listen to counsel, you do not want to listen to anybody. So the Lord smote him with leprosy. That was his judgment. Why? Because he was a novice.

note.label: The Mind of a Child: Void of Ego and Pride

points: Then all the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in the room of his father Amaziah. Keep in mind what tribe Uzziah was. That is why I read verse one. He was Judah.

note.label: Destructive Behaviors Among Our People

points: But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction: for he transgressed against the Lord his God, and went into the temple of the Lord to burn incense upon the altar of incense. So Uzziah became strong. He is not thinking his Most High God was doing this thing, he is thinking he himself is doing this thing. So he becomes very prideful. Now he starts getting big-headed. And he sinned against God, and went into the temple to burn incense. Who was supposed to burn incense? Was it Judah? Levi. So this guy is so prideful and big-headed that he got inside the temple and tried to burn incense.

note.label: Destructive Behaviors Among Our People

points: And Azariah the priest went in after him, and with him fourscore priests of the Lord, that were valiant men: and they withstood Uzziah the king. All the priests said, what are you doing? They withstood him.

note.label: Destructive Behaviors Among Our People

points: And said unto him, It appertaineth not unto thee, Uzziah, to burn incense unto the Lord, but to the priests the sons of Aaron, that are consecrated to burn incense: go out of the sanctuary; for thou hast trespassed; neither shall it be for thine honour from the Lord God. That is not your job to burn incense unto the Lord, that is the priests' job.

note.label: Destructive Behaviors Among Our People

points: Then Uzziah was wroth, and had a censer in his hand to burn incense: and while he was wroth with the priests, the leprosy even rose up in his forehead before the priests in the house of the Lord, from beside the incense altar. So the priests are telling him, get out of here, you are not supposed to be in here burning incense, that is the priests' job. And because he was the king he got angry. And look what the Most High did to him. He covered his body with leprosy.

note.label: Destructive Behaviors Among Our People

points: And Azariah the chief priest, and all the priests, looked upon him, and, behold, he was leprous in his forehead, and they thrust him out from thence; yea, himself hasted also to go out, because the Lord had smitten him. God smote him because of pride.

note.label: Destructive Behaviors Among Our People

points: And Uzziah the king was a leper unto the day of his death. He died a leper. All because of pride. You see what pride can get you?

note.label: Destructive Behaviors Among Our People

points: All the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah. He reigned fifty and two years in Jerusalem and did that which was right in the sight of the Most High.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 26: Uzziah Prospers, Then Pride Brings Him Low

points: He sought the Most High in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the visions of God, and as long as he sought the Most High, God made him to prosper. Prosperity comes from the Most High, and it lasts only as long as a man keeps seeking Him.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 26: Uzziah Prospers, Then Pride Brings Him Low

points: He built towers in Jerusalem and in the desert, dug many wells, and loved husbandry, keeping much cattle and vine dressers. He had a trained host of fighting men, three hundred thousand and seven thousand five hundred that made war with mighty power, and he prepared for them shields, spears, helmets, and engines of war invented by cunning men to shoot arrows and great stones.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 26: Uzziah Prospers, Then Pride Brings Him Low

points: Uzziah went to war against the Philistines, broke down walls, and built cities. God helped him against the Philistines, the Arabians, and the Mehunims, and his name spread abroad, for he was marvellously helped till he was strong.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 26: Uzziah Prospers, Then Pride Brings Him Low

points: But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction. He transgressed against the Most High and went into the temple to burn incense on the altar of incense, which was not his office.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 26: Uzziah Prospers, Then Pride Brings Him Low

points: Azariah the priest and fourscore priests went in after him, withstood him, and told him it did not pertain to him to burn incense but to the priests, the sons of Aaron who are consecrated, and told him to go out of the sanctuary for he had trespassed. Uzziah was wroth, and while he was wroth with a censer in his hand, leprosy rose up in his forehead before the priests.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 26: Uzziah Prospers, Then Pride Brings Him Low

points: The lesson to all of us is to stay in the spirit, stay humble, and never forget who put you in the position you are in. When a man becomes lifted up he loses his humility and forgets who set him where he is. Uzziah was a leper to the day of his death and dwelt in a separate house, cut off from the house of the Most High.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 26: Uzziah Prospers, Then Pride Brings Him Low

points: When Uzziah stayed with the Most High he prospered, and when he departed and did his own thing, going contrary to the laws of God, the Most High made an example of him. He is a warning against thinking of yourself as more than what you are, for a man who thinks he is something when he is nothing deceives himself.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 26: Uzziah Prospers, Then Pride Brings Him Low

points: The rest of the acts of Uzziah, first and last, Isaiah the prophet wrote. Uzziah slept with his fathers and they buried him in the field of burial that belonged to the kings, for they said, He is a leper. Jotham his son reigned in his stead.
